---
title: "Documentation"
description: "How every package's documentation site is built with Great Docs."
---

## 24. Every package has a docs site, built by Great Docs
- Everything about the docs lives in a `docs/` folder: `docs/great-docs.yml` configures the
  site, next to the user guide and any custom sections. `great-docs build` produces a Quarto site
  in `docs/_site/`, which CI deploys to GitHub Pages. (This `docs/` layout is **new**; older
  projects keep these files at the repo root.)
- Great Docs discovers the API from `__all__`. Because of item 14, the API reference stays in
  sync without extra work.
- The `pyproject.toml` `docs` extra installs Great Docs, and the `make docs` / `make docs-preview`
  targets wrap it.

## 25. NumPy-style docstrings with executable examples
- The config sets `parser: numpy`. Docstrings use the standard sections `Parameters`, `Returns`,
  `Raises` and `Examples`, plus custom sections such as `Details` and `Notes`, which render as
  headings.
- **Examples are real Quarto `{python}` cells, not `>>>` doctests.** They run at build time, so
  the docs show actual rendered output: tables, plots, reprs.
  ````
  Examples
  --------
  Let's use the `exibble` dataset to create a table.

  ```{{python}}
  from great_tables import GT, exibble
  GT(exibble).fmt_number(columns="num", decimals=2)
  ```
  ````
- Examples **interleave prose and code cells**: explain a step, show it, explain the next one.
- Examples use the bundled datasets (item 23), so readers can copy and paste them.
- Parameters are documented **by bare name**, with the type left to the signature:
  ```
  Parameters
  ----------
  columns
      The columns to format. ...
  ```
  This is the Great Docs house style. It avoids duplicating annotations, and the signature's
  type hint stays authoritative.
- Docstrings refer to other parameters by name (`decimals=`), and cross-reference functions with
  interlinks: ``[`fmt_number()`](`great_tables.GT.fmt_number`)``.
- Docstrings use Markdown and Quarto markup with single backticks. No RST roles or
  double backticks.

## 26. A curated API reference, not one long alphabetical dump
- `reference:` in `great-docs.yml` groups the API into titled sections, each with a short `desc:`
  (e.g. "Formatting", "Styling", "Export").
- Each section lists its functions, and big classes are split up:
  - `- name: GT` with `members: false`, then the `GT.method` entries listed under their own
    sections.
  - Result classes sit beside the function that produces them (`meta` next to `MetaResult` with
    `members: true`).

## 27. A numbered user guide in Quarto
- `docs/user_guide/` contains numbered `.qmd` files: `00-get-started.qmd`, `01-...`, ...
  `90-glossary.qmd`.
  - The numeric prefix sets the order and is stripped from titles and URLs.
  - High numbers such as `90-` are reserved for back matter like the glossary.
- Pages are grouped into sidebar sections with the `guide-section:` frontmatter key
  ("Getting started", "Core concepts", "Advanced features", ...).
- Nearly every page contains executable `{python}` cells, so the guide is a tested tutorial
  rather than static prose.
- Larger projects add extra sections alongside the guide, such as Examples, Blog or Cookbook
  (via `sections:`). These can be blog-style index pages or have grouped sidebars.

## 28. A designed landing page
- `index.qmd` is written by hand rather than reusing the README:
  - `title: ""`
  - a hero with the logo and tagline
  - a short live (code-folded) example right away
  - a "Why mypkg?" section
- `hero:`, `logo:` (light and dark variants) and `nav_icons:` in the config give each site a
  polished, consistent look.
- The README and `index.qmd` have different jobs. The README is read on GitHub: it introduces
  the repository, with full URLs for links. `docs/index.qmd` is read on the site: it introduces
  the package, can run code, and links to other pages of the site directly. When it exists,
  Great Docs uses it for the homepage instead of the README.

## 29. Commit the freeze cache
- `docs/_freeze/` is committed, so CI doesn't re-run every expensive example on every build. Pages
  re-execute only when their source changes.

## 30. Author, citation and funding metadata on the site
- `authors:` (with ORCID, GitHub and affiliation) and `funding:` (for company-funded projects) in
  `great-docs.yml`, plus `CITATION.cff`, produce an authors page and a citation page.
- A changelog page is built from GitHub Releases automatically, so writing good release notes
  *is* writing the changelog.

## 31. Docs for AI agents: skills and llms.txt
- Great Docs generates `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` on every build, so LLM tools can consume
  the docs.
- The newer projects ship **hand-written `skills/<pkg>/SKILL.md` files** (Pointblank, nokap,
  multimark):
  - They are agent-facing guides with "when to use what" decision tables, the core API, gotchas,
    and error handling.
  - They are registered under `skill:` in `great-docs.yml` and served from
    `.well-known/agent-skills/`.
- Projects with a CLI or an MCP server document those too (the `cli:` and `mcp:` config blocks).

## 32. Docs CI
- On every push to main: install the package plus Great Docs, set up Quarto
  (`quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup`), run `great-docs build`, and deploy with
  `actions/upload-pages-artifact` + `actions/deploy-pages`.
- Great Tables and Pointblank also build **per-PR preview sites**, so reviewers can see the
  rendered docs before merging.
